Katie & Nathaniel: Bonus Features & Behind-the-Scenes Archive

Twenty Archival Dossiers Revealing What Happened Outside Nate's First-Person Point of View (2001–2044)

Read Katie & Nathaniel on RaggieSoft Books ↗ All 57 Backstage Records Copy Link: Read on Phone

Scan with your camera to continue reading this dossier on your phone or tablet.
Story Date & Time 2027-07-22
Setting Virginia Beach, Williamsburg, Fishersville, Richmond, & Danville, Virginia • Maplewood, Minnesota • Windsor, Ontario • Detroit, Michigan • Washington, D.C.

Welcome to the official RaggieSoft Backstage companion archive for Katie & Nathaniel.

Because every chapter of Katie & Nathaniel is written strictly in Nathaniel Prairie's first-person point of view, the main novel only shows what Nate and Katie can directly see, hear, and deduce in the moment. Whenever you encounter a Backstage Bonus Feature button at the end of a chapter on books.raggiesoft.com, you can open these behind-the-scenes dossiers directly inside the reader without breaking narrative immersion.

Complete Chronological Index of Behind-the-Scenes Dossiers (2001–2044)

  1. Oct 19, 2001 — The Sunward Tropics Security File & How Brenda Lost the 'Prairie' Surname
    What happened behind closed doors when Brenda's attorney walked into Arthur Vance's conference room off Independence Boulevard to watch the M/S Sunward Tropics Deck 4 security tape—and how Katie and Nate's request forced Brenda to sign the Va. Code § 20-121.4 stipulation surrendering the Prairie family name and reverting to Brenda Walsh.
  2. Jan 11, 2003 — Five Red X's on the Wall Calendar: Wesley's Perspective on the Morning He Thought He Lost Nate Forever
    Told strictly from fifteen-year-old non-verbal Wesley Collins's third-person limited point of view on Saturday morning, January 11, 2003 in Chesapeake—revealing the sheer terror of having zero phone, bus, or spoken bridge to his very first guy friend Nate when Heather broke up with him, why Wesley blew up in heartbroken protest, and why he rescued the oak-framed November 2001 Annie's Pretzels photo off the living-room shelf to guard beside his bed.
  3. Jan–Jun 2003 — Workstation Three, Cousin Hannah's Green Parka, & Why Heather Knew There Was No Restore Point
    What happened inside Senior Homeroom 212 on January 6 before Heather slammed her locker door, five weeks of Heather sitting alone beside two empty wheelchair spaces in Mr. Callahan's Room 204 lab while Crimson Node's "Unhandled Exception" echoed clear as day inside Nate's head in the back corner, the February 11 cafeteria lunch where Kristen Bauer and the Varsity Girls' Soccer team publicly roasted Tyler out of his seat—making it the last time he ever pulled his fake-cheating pickup stunt and driving him out to lonely Brittany Fletcher at Smoker's Corner—plus Stairway A vs. the middle-loop bus stalls and graduation day at the Virginia Beach Pavilion.
  4. Oct 16–20, 2004 — CBSA Secondary Inspection at 35 Park Street East & The U.S. Marshals File on Brandon Mercer
    Reconstructs what happened between nineteen-year-old Katie and Nate's 4:00 PM six-bus escape from the Williamsburg Transportation Center and Brandon Mercer's arrest by Deputy U.S. Marshals at a men's shelter on Cass Avenue in Detroit—including his ripped-up ticket on East Jefferson Avenue, the Transit Windsor Tunnel Bus farebox trap, his refusal of entry into Canada at 555 Goyeau Street and 35 Park Street East in Windsor, Ontario, and the CBP seizure of his two contraband hard drives on Randolph Street.
  5. Dec 24–27, 2004 — Dirty Old Tonomy Hill & Why Brandon's Tunnel-Bus Scheme Was Doomed Before He Left Williamsburg
    Why developmentally disabled Cousin Chelsea actually held the sole legal authority on the Newport Housing Authority lease to evict Tiffany Sloan from her apartment on Tonomy Hill while locking Katie and Nate safely inside her bedroom—plus the two rail and cross-border bus tariff rules Brandon Mercer never bothered to read before leaving Williamsburg.
  6. Mar 8–15, 2007 — The Unopened RRC Staff Dossier: Form A vs. Form B & The Unsigned Level 1 Contract
    Opens the internal Bates-Harding staff notes on "Prairie, Nathaniel" and "Prairie, Katie"—revealing why Ms. Hollis and Mr. Miller separated their tests into Form A and Form B expecting them to cheat on the outdated 1996 exam battery, why VITA locked down the lab on Quantum OS 2000 Professional, and the drafted Level 1 Restriction & Mandatory Separation Contract sitting on their counselor's desk on Thursday morning.
  7. Mar 13, 2007 — The 11:00 PM Curfew Search & Why Locking the Seasonal Closet Door Got Nate and Katie Caught
    Discover how Barton Hall dorm staff tracked Nate and Katie to the Rec Hall without an on-campus sign-out sheet—and why locking a normally unlocked door in a notorious student hookup closet is the exact thing that tipped the night supervisor off while the twins were hidden in the dark.
  8. Mar 14–15, 2007 — How Christopher Vance Scrambled the Dorm Roster & The Thursday Morning Cover-Up
    What happened behind closed doors when Christopher Vance stole an open administrative login to swap opposite-gender dorm room assignments on Wednesday night, why RRC whisked him onto a bus in Staunton at 7:50 AM on Thursday without calling the State Police, and why Nate and Katie's 10:00 AM Level 1 disciplinary counselor meeting never happened.
  9. Oct 28, 2010 — The 509 East 18th Street Executive Suite, Mayor Overton's Bus, & Harold Dietz's 0.4% Collapse
    Why CVTA CEO Leonard Sterling and COO Richard Halstead blackballed Nate from TRAC, the real Tidewater municipal history of the Newtown Road bus-border cliff that haunted Mayor Myra E. Overton, why Incumbent Councilman Harold Dietz left his debate podium empty on WHRC TV-15, and the internal tracking poll (44.6% to 44.2%) that triggered his fatal WTGA 790 AM radio attack on Katie's wheelchair ramp.
  10. Feb 4, 2016 — Majority Leader Callaway's Closed-Door Post-Mortem on HB 663 & The Pre-Floor Review That Never Happened
    What happened inside House Majority Leader Richard "Uncle Richard" Callaway's (R-Danville) Capitol office thirty minutes after HB 663 imploded on the floor—and the step-by-step pre-floor bill review in Room 518 with Katie and the thirteen-year-old Hawkins triplets (Sarah, Mandy, and Sam) that would have spared Delegate Martin Cobb his televised humiliation.
  11. Spring 2003 – Mar 2016 — From Smoker's Corner to Hillside Court: How Tyler Trapped Brittany on a Joint Lease & How Delegate Prairie Helped Her Exit Above Board
    How the February 2003 Varsity Soccer roast drove radioactive sleazebag Tyler out to lonely Brittany Fletcher at Smoker's Corner—talking her into dropping out at eighteen, dragging her onto a joint Hillside Court public-housing lease when her car died in 2013, her Friday midday JRTC ride without an appointment ("Hold the elevator!"), and how Delegate Katie Prairie stayed 100% ethically above board while getting Brittany's name severed mid-lease via Va. Code § 55-248.21:2, federal VAWA lease bifurcation, and Central Virginia Legal Aid.
  12. Feb 5–6, 2016 — Why the House Page Triplets Bolted From Room 518 & How Uncle Richard Rescued Them
    Reveals how Uncle Richard Callaway and Aunt Marge rescued thirteen-year-old autistic triplets Sam, Mandy, and Sarah Hawkins in early 2015, why the triplets bolted from the doorway of Room 518 during Katie and Nate's Friday morning meltdown to fetch both Floor Leaders, and how Saturday Night Sketch (Studio 6B) wrote the viral HB 663 cold open without "cripping up."
  13. Feb–Jun 2016 — Maplewood Living Room: Wesley Sees Katie on TV & Heather's Cautious Grid Request
    Inside Heather and Dan Lindstrom's Maplewood home on Sunday morning, February 7, 2016, when twenty-eight-year-old Wesley Collins—quietly sad over twelve years of missing postcards—explodes with joy spotting Katie and Nate on Meet the Nation, tries to understand state government, and convinces Heather to send a humble, zero-pressure Message Request on The Grid.
  14. Jun 16, 2018 — Architectural Blueprint & Visitor Guide: Inside North Lion Scales & Tails (Maplewood, MN)
    Complete illustrated cutaway floor plan of Heather and Dan's barrier-free Route 64 facility—from the zero-step automatic sliding front doors, Front Customer Service Counter & registers, Supply Store, Adoption Center, and Dr. Meyer's Exotic Pets Vet Clinic to the Skylit Greenhouse Conservatory (turtles & tortoises), Reptile Galleries, and Small Mammal Meadow.
  15. Jun 16, 2018 (10:28–10:48 AM CDT) — While the Classroom Door Was Closed: Staff Member Wesley, Cousin Chelsea, & Matching Blue Gloves at the Turtle Lagoon
    Stays out in the sunlit North Lion Scales & Tails conservatory while Nate, Katie, and Heather talk privately inside the Education Classroom—following thirty-one-year-old Staff Member Wesley and thirty-six-year-old Cousin Chelsea in matching light-blue animal-care gloves as they feed Clover, Scooter, and Barnaby together beside Brittany, Dan, Jonas, Nora, and Molly.
  16. Jun 16, 2018 — Alternate 'What If' Dossier: Marriage in the North Star State — And Why Brittany & Chelsea Would Never Have Been Rescued
    Traces what would have happened if Tyler's 2003 lie had never ended Nate and Heather (or if the twins had taken Heather back at graduation): a loving marriage and software life in Minnesota sparing Katie and Nate from Brandon and Tiffany, at the devastating butterfly-effect cost of never rescuing Cousin Brittany in South Richmond or Cousin Chelsea in Rhode Island.
  17. Jun 2026 – Jan 2027 — The $14 Million DSCC Primary Shock, Backing Chris Van Deren Over Schuman, The 211–204 Lame-Duck False Dawn, & The Senate Wheelchair Caucus
    Inside retiring Senator Martin Warren's office and the DSCC when Katie and Nate's bus-riding campaign defeated Preston Holloway, Uncle Richard going live on Beacon News from Danville to defend Katie against President Garrett Thorne, Katie backing Senator Chris Van Deren (D-MD) in his 29–26 caucus upset over Senator Charles Schuman (D-NY), Defense Secretary Bret Halverson's premature "total victory" lap after escaping impeachment on a 211–204 lame-duck referral vote, the Architect of the Capitol's desk upgrades for the three-member U.S. Senate Wheelchair Caucus (Senator Tess Dunmore [D-IL], Senator Katie Prairie [D-VA], and Senator Josh Novak [D-IA]), and Vice President Conrad Drayton's fury in S-216 over swearing Katie in on the U.S. Constitution.
  18. Feb 16, 2027 — Inside Dirksen Room 511: Commissioner Sterling & Director Cross's Panic
    Follow the nine stages of bureaucratic collapse inside Dirksen Room 511 as DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and RRC Director Evelyn Cross wonder how a United States Senator knows the exact color of 2007 Level 2 Barton Hall passes, the MedStrip wound-closure strips on a girl's broken nose, and the lumpy bags of curtains inside a Rec Hall storage closet—until the math clicks (41 - 20 = 21) and Governor's Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence reads them the Riot Act from Richmond.
  19. Jul 22, 2027 (9:03–10:25 AM) — Governor Langford's Capitol Square Reckoning With Commissioner Sterling & Secretary Alcott
    What happened inside the Patrick Henry Building on Capitol Square twenty minutes after Katie called Governor Rebecca Langford on speakerphone from Fishersville—as a volcanically irate Governor confronts DARS Commissioner Marcus Sterling and Secretary of Health and Human Resources Dr. Miriam Alcott with Sterling's June 14 "wait out the July markup" email, lays two manila folders (5:00 PM Resignation vs. Va. Code § 2.2-106 Removal for Cause) on her mahogany table, keeps Secretary Alcott on an ice-cold final warning, and elevates Acting DARS Commissioner Angela Thornton.
  20. Jul 22, 2027 (12:38–8:15 PM) — Arthur Lawrence's Fishersville Sweep, VITA's 120-Day Unsigned Form, & The 5:00 PM Resignations
    Follow Chief of Staff Arthur Lawrence, State Inspector General Kenneth Dalton, VITA CIO Rajiv Patel, and Acting Commissioner Angela Thornton up I-64 into Fishersville at 12:38 PM—uncovering VITA's approved March 24 classroom VLAN form that Dr. Cross left unsigned for 120 days, unlocking all twelve lab workstations live by 4:15 PM, pulling lobby security video of Assistant Director Greg Saunders grabbing twenty-year-old Marcus's wheelchair push-handles alongside a June purchase order for 5,000 yellow passes, and securing Cross's and Saunders's resignations before 5:00 PM in lieu of Group III termination.
  21. Mar 2029 — Architectural & Family Guide: Three Mirrored Ground-Floor In-Law Suites — Virginia Beach, Alexandria, & Maplewood
    How David, Katie, Nate, Brittany, Heather, and Dan build three inch-for-inch mirrored zero-step ground-floor in-law suites once Senator Katie Prairie's 2028 Supported Companions, Waiver Portability, and Social Security Solvency Act takes effect—connected directly via oak pocket doors to 737 Arvin Road in Virginia Beach and Sunset Drive in Alexandria, and via a heated cedar breezeway to Heather & Dan's home on TCT Route 64 in Maplewood—so Wesley Collins and Chelsea Prairie live together year-round under full guardian support.
  22. Mar 2027 – Spring 2044 — Brenda Walsh's Suite 756 Cease-and-Desist, Thorne's Gag Order, & The 2044 Route 15 Bus-Stop Primary
    The complete story behind Brenda Walsh's unauthorized Tidewater Thorne & RTR Superstore in Suite 756 at Timberline Shopping Center (shut down by a Cease-and-Desist letter from Thorne Enterprises ten days after her own daughter voted to convict and bar Garrett Thorne for life), how a federal bail gag order (18 U.S.C. § 3142) silenced Thorne, and why fifty-eight-year-old three-term Senator Katie Prairie refused the 2044 Presidential Nomination at the CVTA Route #15 bus stop and forced every White House contender to interview on a live Virginia Beach transit loop ("Wait—a bus? Huh?!").
